summary: The investigation could not definitively identify a root cause for the repeated OOMKilled restarts of notification-service. Verified observations show sharp memory usage spikes (>90%) and consumer lag spikes preceding each OOM event, but no concrete link to recent changes or external factors could be established. Confidence in a root‑cause conclusion is low; further data collection is required.

facts.statement: Three OOMKilled restarts of notification-service occurred at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z.

Memory usage (memory_pct) of notification-service rose sharply from ~48% on 2026-03-20 to >90% just before each OOM event, peaking at 94.55% (2026-03-21T18:15:00Z), 97.98% (2026-03-22T20:15:00Z), and 95.16% (2026-03-23T15:45:00Z).
After each OOM restart, memory_pct dropped back to ~53‑63%.
Consumer lag for notification-service spiked dramatically before each OOM event (avg ~520‑556, max >17k).
No configuration changes were recorded for notification-service between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-23.
order-service showed no OOMKilled logs and its memory_pct remained stable (~60%).
Historical incident HIST-104 (2025-11-05) involved notification-service and Kafka with consumer lag spikes caused by a Kafka partition reassignment storm.

assumptions: The in‑memory template cache deployment (dep-5402) actually increased memory pressure on notification-service.
Kafka maintenance performed on 2026-03-23 could have caused a replay that increased consumer lag.
No other services besides order-service experienced OOM events during the same window.
(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) A deployment (dep-5402) adding an in‑memory template cache was applied to notification-service on 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z (unverified).

timeline.event: Deployment dep-5402 adding an in‑memory template cache applied to notification-service (unverified).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back deployment dep-5402 (remove in‑memory template cache) and monitor memory usage.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cache deployment coincides with the start of the OOM pattern and could be adding memory pressure.

recommended_actions.action: Increase memory limits / request for notification-service pod and enable memory‑usage alerts.
recommended_actions.rationale: Observed memory_pct consistently exceeds 90% before OOM; higher limits may prevent immediate kills while root cause is investigated.

recommended_actions.action: Collect and verify runtime metrics (memory, CPU, GC, consumer lag) for notification-service and Kafka during the next maintenance window.
recommended_actions.rationale: Current gaps prevent correlation of OOM events with Kafka activity or lag spikes.

recommended_actions.action: Obtain detailed Kafka maintenance logs (timing, partitions affected) and compare with OOM timestamps.
recommended_actions.rationale: To test the hypothesis that Kafka replay after maintenance caused lag and memory spikes.

recommended_actions.action: Audit upstream (email-provider) and downstream (Kafka) configuration changes between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-23.
recommended_actions.rationale: Missing change data could hide a contributing factor.

recommended_actions.action: Implement finer‑grained consumer lag monitoring (sub‑minute resolution) for notification-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: Current lag metric granularity (≈9.7 h) is insufficient to pinpoint spikes at OOM moments.

recommended_actions.action: Add automated regression testing for memory usage when new in‑memory caches are introduced.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future deployments that unintentionally increase memory pressure.

data_gaps: No runtime metric data (memory usage, OOMKilled events, consumer lag) for notification-service or Kafka around the OOM incidents was collected.
Deployments and configuration changes for upstream/downstream services (Kafka, email-provider) were not retrieved.
Details of the Kafka maintenance window (timing, scope) were not obtained.
Consumer lag metric is bucketed at ~9.7 h, limiting precise correlation with OOM timestamps.
No Kafka maintenance logs were found for the period 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-24.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Verified evidence that the in‑memory template cache added by dep-5402 directly caused memory usage to exceed pod limits.
Confirmed Kafka maintenance logs showing a replay that produced the observed consumer lag spikes immediately before each OOM event.
Discovery of a configuration change in the email‑provider that increased payload size, leading to higher memory consumption in notification-service.
